```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 10_confidence_intervals_learning_checks
title: >
  Learning Checks
questions:
  - id: expected_z_null
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      On average across many studies, what value of z would you expect if the null
      hypothesis is true each time?
    options:
      - text: >
          0
        correct: true
      - text: >
          1
      - text: >
          The critical value
      - text: >
          The sample size
    explanation: >
      If the null is true, the expected difference in the numerator is zero.

  - id: significant_z_factors
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      Which combination is most likely to produce a significant z statistic?
    options:
      - text: >
          Large mean difference, small variability, large n
        correct: true
      - text: >
          Small mean difference, large variability, small n
      - text: >
          Large variability and small n only
      - text: >
          A large p-value
    explanation: >
      A larger numerator and smaller standard error of the mean produce a larger
      absolute z value.

  - id: single_study_z_null
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      In a single study, what absolute value of z is most expected if the null
      hypothesis is true?
    options:
      - text: >
          A value near 0
        correct: true
      - text: >
          A value beyond the critical value
      - text: >
          Exactly 1.96 every time
      - text: >
          Exactly the sample size
    explanation: >
      Random samples vary, but values near zero are most common under the null.
```
